# Sheet

A panel that stays open over a full-bleed canvas like a map: a floating card on a wide container, a bottom sheet with three detents on a narrow one. Unlike Drawer, it never blocks the page.

```tsx
<div className="relative h-[30rem]">
  {/* your map, board or canvas */}
  <Sheet size="sm">
    <SheetHandle />
    <SheetHeader>
      <SheetTitle>Nearby</SheetTitle>
      <SheetDescription>Five places open now, closest first.</SheetDescription>
    </SheetHeader>
    <SheetBody>
      <List variant="plain">…</List>
    </SheetBody>
    <SheetFooter>
      <Button variant="ghost" className="flex-1">Filters</Button>
      <Button className="flex-1">Directions</Button>
    </SheetFooter>
  </Sheet>
</div>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli@latest init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli@latest add sheet
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/sheet/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

Put the Sheet inside the positioned element it floats over, usually the box your map fills. It is absolute in there, and that element is what it measures: wider than `breakpoint` (768px by default) it floats as a card, narrower it rises from the bottom. It follows the container, not the viewport, so it behaves the same full-screen and inside a panel.

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import {
  Sheet, SheetHandle, SheetHeader, SheetTitle,
  SheetDescription, SheetBody, SheetFooter,
} from "@/components/ui/sheet"

export function MapScreen() {
  return (
    <div className="relative h-dvh">
      <Map className="absolute inset-0" />
      <Sheet>
        <SheetHandle />
        <SheetHeader>
          <SheetTitle>Nearby</SheetTitle>
          <SheetDescription>Five places open now.</SheetDescription>
        </SheetHeader>
        <SheetBody>{/* … */}</SheetBody>
        <SheetFooter>{/* … */}</SheetFooter>
      </Sheet>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Detents

On a narrow canvas the sheet rests at one of three heights: `peek` (the header and a row or two, `peekHeight` sets it), `half`, and `full`, which leaves a strip of the canvas visible at the top. Drag the handle or the header and let go: the release velocity is projected, so a flick carries it to the next detent. A tap on the handle steps it up. Control it with `detent` and `onDetentChange`, or let it start at `defaultDetent`.

```tsx
const [detent, setDetent] = React.useState<SheetDetent>("half")

<Sheet detent={detent} onDetentChange={setDetent}>
  <SheetHandle />
  <SheetHeader>…</SheetHeader>
  <SheetBody>…</SheetBody>
</Sheet>
```

## Side and size

The floating card docks to the `left` (the default) or `right` edge, top to bottom with a margin all round. `size` picks its width on the same steps Drawer uses (`sm`, `md` by default, `lg`, `xl`); a width class of your own replaces it. A bottom sheet always spans the canvas.

```tsx
<Sheet side="right" size="sm" density="compact">
  <SheetHandle />
  <SheetHeader>
    <SheetTitle>Layers</SheetTitle>
    <SheetDescription>What the map draws on top of the streets.</SheetDescription>
  </SheetHeader>
  <SheetBody>…</SheetBody>
</Sheet>
```

## The visible area

A map centred on the whole canvas puts half of what you look at under the sheet. `onInsetChange` reports how much of the canvas the sheet covers, per edge and in pixels, every time that changes (the layout, the detent, the width, and each frame of a drag). Hand it to the map as padding and it centres things in the part that is still visible.

```tsx
<Sheet onInsetChange={(insets) => map.setPadding(insets)}>
  …
</Sheet>
```

## Keyboard and screen readers

The Sheet is a named `<aside>`, a complementary landmark, labelled by its `SheetTitle` (or pass an `aria-label`). Nothing traps focus and nothing behind it goes inert: it is part of the page. On a bottom sheet the handle is a focusable window splitter: ArrowUp and ArrowDown step between detents, Home and End jump to `peek` and `full`, Enter and Space step it up, and it announces the detent through `aria-valuetext` (rename them with `detentLabels`).

## API reference

### Sheet

An absolute `<aside>` that measures its parent: at or above `breakpoint` it floats as a card, below it rises as a bottom sheet with three detents. Forwards all native `<aside>` props, and every part accepts `className`, merged last.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| detent | "peek" \| "half" \| "full" | - | The bottom sheet's detent (controlled). |
| defaultDetent | "peek" \| "half" \| "full" | "half" | The detent it starts at when uncontrolled. |
| onDetentChange | (detent: SheetDetent) => void | - | Called when a drag, tap, key or `setDetent` moves the detent. |
| side | "left" \| "right" | "left" | The edge the floating card docks to. |
| size | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" | "md" | The floating card's width on the container scale; a bottom sheet always spans the canvas. |
| breakpoint | number | 768 | Canvas width (px) at and above which the sheet floats. |
| peekHeight | number | 176 | Height (px) of the `peek` detent: the header and a row or two. |
| onInsetChange | (insets: SheetInsets) => void | - | Reports how much of the canvas the sheet covers per edge (`top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left`, in px), on every layout, detent or width change and every drag frame. |
| density | "compact" \| "comfortable" | "compact" | Padding and title size of the parts. Falls back to the nearest `DensityProvider` and passes it on to the content. |

| Data attribute | Description |
| --- | --- |
| data-layout | `floating` or `bottom`; absent for the first frame, while the canvas is measured (the sheet stays invisible). |
| data-detent | The current detent, on a bottom sheet only. |
| data-dragging | Present while a finger or pointer is dragging the sheet. |
| data-side | `left` or `right`. |

### SheetHandle

The bottom sheet's grab bar and keyboard control, a focusable `role="separator"`: ArrowUp and ArrowDown step detents, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter, Space or a tap step it up. Renders nothing while the sheet floats; forwards all native `<div>` props.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| detentLabels | Partial<Record<SheetDetent, string>> | { peek: "Peek", half: "Half height", full: "Full height" } | What the handle announces for each detent as its `aria-valuetext`, for your language. |
| aria-label | string | "Resize the sheet" | The handle's accessible name. |

### SheetHeader

The title block. On a bottom sheet it is also a drag region, so the whole top can be grabbed. Forwards all native `<div>` props.

### SheetTitle

An `<h2>`; the sheet is labelled by it unless the Sheet gets an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Forwards all native `<h2>` props.

### SheetDescription

Muted supporting text under the title. Forwards all native `<p>` props.

### SheetBody

The scrollable content between header and footer. Forwards all native `<div>` props.

### SheetFooter

A row pinned to the sheet's bottom edge, the place for a tab bar or the primary action. A lone child fills it; give several `flex-1` to share it. Forwards all native `<div>` props.

### useSheet

A hook for anything inside the Sheet: returns `{ layout, detent, setDetent }`, where `layout` is `"floating"`, `"bottom"` or `null` before the first measure.

## FAQ

### When should I use a Sheet instead of a Drawer?

Use a Drawer for a task that interrupts: it opens over the page, dims it, traps focus and closes when you are done. Use a Sheet for a panel that lives next to the page for as long as the page is open, like the place list over a map or the layers of a design board. The Sheet never dims, traps or closes; the canvas under it stays fully usable.

### Why does it follow the container width and not the viewport?

Because the Sheet lives inside the canvas it covers, and that canvas is not always the whole window: a map inside a dashboard pane is narrow on a wide screen. Measuring the container (with a ResizeObserver) picks the right shape wherever it is placed, including a docs preview. Change the switch point with `breakpoint`.

### How do I keep a map centred on what is still visible?

Pass `onInsetChange` and hand its insets to the map as padding, for example `map.setPadding(insets)` in MapLibre or Mapbox. It fires when the layout, detent or width changes and on each frame of a drag, so the map follows the sheet as it moves.

### Can I render something only on the bottom sheet, or at a given detent?

Yes: inside the Sheet, `useSheet()` returns the current `layout` (`floating` or `bottom`) and `detent`, plus `setDetent`. Use it to show a compact summary at `peek`, or to move to `full` when a search field gets focus.

### Where does an app's tab bar go?

In `SheetFooter`. It is pinned to the sheet's bottom edge, which on a bottom sheet is the canvas's own bottom edge, so the bar stays in reach at every detent while the body scrolls above it. A lone child fills the footer, so the bar spans the sheet without a width of its own; several children sit side by side, so give them `flex-1` to share the row.

- Components and helpers: `Sheet`, `SheetHandle`, `SheetHeader`, `SheetTitle`, `SheetDescription`, `SheetBody`, `SheetFooter`, `useSheet`, `sheetVariants`
- Types: `SheetProps`, `SheetHandleProps`, `SheetDetent`, `SheetLayout`, `SheetSide`, `SheetInsets`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `create-context`, `density`, `tv`, `utils`
